body.statement: For every \(C=(G,\Pi),D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathfrak S_p\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\); \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\), equivalently \(G,H\) have the same skeleton and unshielded colliders, \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for all \(j\in V\), and every edge joining vertices with unequal nonsingleton families has the same orientation; and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\). Every step in the final characterization is a partition-compatible singleton covered reversal with the prescribed transport. Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\), and a shortest path reverses each disagreeing arrow exactly once. When no parent block of \(C\) is a singleton, \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), agreeing with the BPEC structural-identifiability theorem on its proper no-singleton subclass. The preceding equivalence criterion applies to the published blocked superclass that also permits singleton blocks.
body.justification: The theorem identifies the exact full-model quotient on the published singleton-permitting blocked class and gives both its static recovery functional and its legal local transformation calculus.
body.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves uniqueness only inside the proper no-singleton BPEC subclass and asks for edge-coloured equivalence; Chickering1995 has no coefficient-partition legality condition.
body.consumer: An extension of the colouredDAGs workflow can report the exact covariance-equivalence component while retaining every repeated-coefficient community.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(C=(G,\Pi)\) and \(D=(H,\Lambda)\) in \(\mathfrak S_p\). By \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\), both graphs are finite labelled DAGs and each displayed family is a partition of the corresponding parent set. By \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\), all block coefficients range over \(\mathbb R\), every innovation variance lies in \((0,\infty)\), and \(\mathcal M(E)\) is the full positive-definite covariance image of the SEM. Thus the causal object to be recovered is the graph--partition state up to \(\mathcal R(C)\), whereas equality of the observable full-model images is the identifying relation to be proved equivalent to it.

Suppose first that
\[
 \mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D).
\]
The result \(\texttt{lem:edge-coloured-model-equivalence-markov}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{skel}(G)=\operatorname{skel}(H),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{uc}(G)=\operatorname{uc}(H).
\]
The already established tangent-support result \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\) gives, vertex by vertex,
\[
 \mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D),\qquad j\in V.
\]
Consider an adjacency \(\{x,y\}\) whose orientations in \(G\) and \(H\) differ. The already established sparse-separator result \(\texttt{lem:reversed-edge-separator}\) yields
\[
 \mathcal N_x(C)=\mathcal N_y(C).
\]
Taking the contrapositive, every adjacency whose endpoint families are unequal has the same orientation in \(G\) and \(H\). Since the skeleton and the vertex-indexed families agree, the definition \(\texttt{def:family-mismatch-edges}\) therefore gives \(F(C)=F(D)\). All four coordinates in \(\texttt{def:static-signature}\) agree, so
\[
 \mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D).
\]

Conversely, suppose \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\). Equality of the first two signature coordinates and \(\texttt{lem:verma-pearl-markov-equivalence}\) show that \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent. Put
\[
 \mathcal N_j:=\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D),\qquad j\in V.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:chickering-monotone-covered-reversals}\), there is a sequence
\[
 G=G_0,G_1,\ldots,G_r=H,
 \qquad r=\delta(C,D),
\]
in which \(G_{t+1}\) is obtained from \(G_t\) by reversing one covered arrow that disagrees with \(H\); the reversed underlying edges are distinct, and every intermediate graph is an acyclic member of the same Markov-equivalence class.

We lift this sequence inductively. Let \(E_t=(G_t,\Pi^t)\) be the current blocked state and assume
\[
 \mathcal N_k(E_t)=\mathcal N_k,\qquad k\in V.
\]
This holds for \(t=0\). Suppose the selected covered arrow is \(i\to j\). It is one of the original arrows on which \(G\) and \(H\) disagree. If \(\mathcal N_i\neq\mathcal N_j\), that arrow belongs to \(F(C)\), and equality \(F(C)=F(D)\) forces the same orientation in \(G\) and \(H\), a contradiction. Hence
\[
 \mathcal N_i=\mathcal N_j=:\mathcal N.
\]
Let \(B\in\Pi^t_j\) be the unique block containing \(i\). If \(|B|\geq2\), then \(B\in\mathcal N_j(E_t)=\mathcal N\). Equality of the endpoint families implies \(B\in\mathcal N_i(E_t)\), and every member of the latter family is a subset of \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(i)\). But \(i\in B\), which would make \(i\) its own parent. A DAG has no self-loop, so this is impossible. Therefore
\[
 B=\{i\},
 \qquad \{i\}\in\Pi^t_j.
\]

Coveredness says
\[
 P:=\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(i)
   =\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(j)\setminus\{i\}.
\]
Let \(U=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal N}A\). The nonsingleton blocks at \(i\) and \(j\) are exactly \(\mathcal N\). If \(k\in P\setminus U\), the block containing \(k\) in either target partition cannot have size at least two, for then it would belong to \(\mathcal N\) and put \(k\) in \(U\). Thus that block is \(\{k\}\) in both partitions. Consequently
\[
 \Pi^t_i=\mathcal N\cup\bigl\{\{k\}:k\in P\setminus U\bigr\},
\]
and, using the already proved singleton status of \(i\to j\),
\[
 \Pi^t_j=\mathcal N\cup\bigl\{\{k\}:k\in P\setminus U\bigr\}
                 \cup\{\{i\}\}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \Pi^t_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^t_i.
\]
The three conditions in \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\) now hold. Applying \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\) gives a state \(E_{t+1}\) with graph \(G_{t+1}\); by \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\), it preserves all nonsingleton families, so the induction continues.

After \(r\) steps the graph is \(H\). A parent set \(P_j\) and a compatible nonsingleton family \(\mathcal N_j\) determine the entire partition uniquely:
\[
 \mathcal N_j\cup
 \left\{\{k\}:k\in P_j\setminus
       \bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j}B\right\}.
\]
The final state and \(D\) have the same graph \(H\) and the same nonsingleton families, so their partitions both equal this display. Thus the final state is \(D\), proving \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\).

If instead \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\), the definition \(\texttt{def:reversal-component}\) supplies a finite legal-reversal sequence from \(C\) to \(D\). Repeated application of \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\) gives equality of the covariance-model image at every step, hence
\[
 \mathcal M(D)=\mathcal M(C).
\]
This proves equivalence of all three criteria.

The lifted Chickering sequence has \(\delta(C,D)\) steps and reverses each disagreeing edge once. Conversely, each legal move reverses only one skeleton edge. Every edge oriented differently in the endpoints must be reversed an odd, hence positive, number of times along any path. Therefore every legal path has length at least \(\delta(C,D)\), and
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D).
\]

It remains to check the proper-block boundary and the edge fact used by the canonical reduction. For any \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) and \(i\in B\), one has \(i\to j\) in \(G\). Equality \(\mathcal N_i(C)=\mathcal N_j(C)\) would imply \(B\in\mathcal N_i(C)\), hence \(i\in\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\), which is impossible. Thus
\[
 B\in\mathcal N_j(C),\ i\in B
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 i\to j\in F(C).
\]
If no block is a singleton, every edge is covered by the first premise in this display. Hence every arrow belongs to \(F(C)\) and is fixed by the static criterion. The fixed graph and fixed nonsingleton families determine every partition, so \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\). This is exactly the BPEC conclusion supplied by \(\texttt{lem:bpec-proper-identifiability}\) on the proper no-singleton subclass. The larger class \(\mathfrak S_p\) is the published blocked superclass with singleton blocks admitted; its nontrivial components are characterized by the equivalence just proved, not by transferring the BPEC converse beyond its stated class.
